freshness.note: Newest inventory 2026-07-16; the two ZenithMind proof libraries were last modified 2026-04-13/14, over four months ago. These are FILE MODIFICATION dates — neither library carries an internal date — so "last updated in April" is an inference from the filesystem. Copy risks being written from stale proof.

captureMechanism.note: Nothing running. Not found across 49 forms, 476 workflows and 470 tags (plus 13 surveys, 186 custom fields, 964 email templates and 495 campaigns, each paginated to its reported total). IMPORTANT: those object types all sit inside GoHighLevel — the mechanism that actually produced SP's 115 testimonials was OUTSIDE it, a cohort contest form run by hand, which lapsed after the spring cohorts. The finding is "it stopped", not "it never existed". Re-checked live every refresh, so this flips by itself the day an in-platform one is built. THE CONSTRAINT.

frontEndAsk.note: 168 unique contacts across the four First Imprint buyer tags (100+67+7+4 rows, deduped by email), and not one was asked how it went. Sits below Stripe's 174 registration units — that gap is the buyer-tagging defect, not a different population. The largest buyer group SP has is never asked.

emergingMechanism.note: Ashley's 2026-08-17 guarantee ruling accidentally built what this stage is missing: to qualify, a ZenithMind buyer must complete all four lessons AND SUBMIT RESULTS — a documented win, from a named customer, at the moment they are most pleased. ZenithMind-only, and the submission channel is owned (Camilla) but not built. Widening it to the front end is the cheapest Advocate fix available.
